newsitem.title: CHINA: China Opium War film to press UK to admit mistakes.
newsitem.headline: China Opium War film to press UK to admit mistakes.

text.p: Chinese movie director Xie Jin said on Monday he hopes his new film, "The Opium War", about Britain's 1840-42 conflict with China, will make the British face up to their mistakes ahead of the Hong Kong handover.
Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, was ceded to Britain at the end of the first Opium War, sparked by Britain's sale of opium to China.
"A country has its glories, but it also has mistakes," Xie said. "British history has glories but it also has bad things."

Xie compared the Opium War to Japanese militarism in the 1930s, Germany's massacre of Jews during World War Two and China's own Cultural Revolution from 1966-1976, saying all countries had shameful periods of history.
The director, best known for making officially sanctioned movies, denied that "The Opium War" was a propaganda film.
"My viewpoint was to make a big film, a profound film," Xie said. "I wanted to make a fair movie, an historical movie about the Opium War."
Xie said the money for the 100 million yuan ($12 million) film did not come from the Chinese government but from various Chinese companies, which Xie declined to name.
"I choose which movies I film," he said. "My movies are not dictated by the leaders."
The film was shot partially in Britain using British actors with one-third of the dialogue in English, Xie said.
"This is China giving England a better chance for cooperation," he said. "I hope the English people will accept it."

The film will be released in June for showing in China's major cities as well as Hong Kong ahead of the handover. Distributors in South Korea, Malyasia, Singapore and Thailand have also signed agreements to show the film.
The movie will be shown to potential distributors on May 8 and 12 in Cannes. The film has has not been entered for the Cannes Film Festival.
